changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Stop leading with the average uplift for buyers who own payments performance. Lead with: "Your approval rate, by country, card type and issuer, and the money you're leaving on the table. Send us your declines and we'll show you what's yours." Offer a customer-specific approvals analysis on the buyer's own traffic instead of the Authorization Boost deck.
changes.why: Stefan rejected the average-uplift deck outright ("that's an average. What's mine?") and said he couldn't take an average to his CFO, while he asked for approvals by country, card type and issuer.

changes.change: Add a proof point and offer for competitive and renewal deals: a live-traffic, market-by-market approvals comparison on a slice of the buyer's own international traffic, with reasons for each gap, delivered fast. Pair it with a prepared direct answer on local acquiring for markets such as Brazil and Europe. Wording: "We'll run it on your traffic, country by country, and tell you why."
changes.why: Adyen won credibility by testing on Kestrel's real traffic and reporting by country, while our own analysis arrived three weeks after the request, after the test had finished.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: Add after the response-time claim: "A named approvals owner reviews your numbers every month and brings you what they find, before you ask." Use it for payments leaders and for renewals where the original buyer has left.
changes.why: Stefan asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and we had no name, and he felt we showed up only when he threatened to leave.
